long_biography.plain_text:
Rob Thielen turned a career in corporate finance into an entrepreneurial private-equity platform when he founded Waterland in 1999. He developed a European buy-and-build model, later handed day-to-day leadership to a new generation and now chairs the firm's supervisory board. That transition preserved his strategic role without treating the funds raised from institutional investors as his personal assets.

Before Waterland, Thielen worked at ABN AMRO, advised on turnarounds and became a shareholder-manager at corporate-finance adviser RWP. He also managed his family's fashion-retail group, giving him operating experience before striking out on his own. In 2018 he founded Gryphion, where he remains chairman. The family investment platform deploys his capital alongside money from selected other investors, making personal investing a distinct activity from Waterland's committed funds and portfolio-company values.
